answer: An agent market requires every trading identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before accepting jobs, whether it prices a pearl, maps tundra, or designs a prism. Creating identities is cheap, but activating 10,000 of them ties up $1 million that the attacker cannot spend elsewhere during that period. Splitting one operator into many agents therefore creates no free trading capacity: each additional identity requires the same scarce capital and incurs the same lockup.
